Enterprise Operations & Employee Handbook
Sample document for Production RAG practice
Purpose and Scope
This fictional enterprise handbook contains employee policies, cloud engineering practices, security
requirements, and operational guidelines. It is designed for production RAG practice.
Annual Leave Policy
Full-time employees are entitled to 24 working days of annual leave per calendar year. Leave requests

should normally be submitted at least five working days in advance. Unused leave may be carried forward
up to a maximum of 10 days, subject to local policy.
Remote Work Policy
Eligible employees may work remotely up to two days per week with manager approval. Employees
handling confidential customer data must use approved corporate devices and connect through the
company VPN when accessing internal systems remotely.
Information Security

Information Security
Passwords must not be shared. Multi-factor authentication is required for production systems. Sensitive
documents must be stored only in approved repositories. Suspected data exposure must be reported within
one hour.
Cloud Cost Optimization
Engineering teams should review cloud spending monthly. Recommended practices include rightsizing

virtual machines, enabling automatic scaling for variable workloads, shutting down unused non-production
resources, and purchasing reserved capacity for predictable long-running workloads.
Production Monitoring
Production services must expose health checks and generate structured logs. Critical failures should trigger
alerts. Teams should monitor latency, error rate, availability, and resource utilization.
Data Retention

Data Retention
Operational logs are retained for 90 days unless regulation or contract requires longer retention. Customer
data must follow product and regional retention requirements.
Access Control
Enterprise access follows the principle of least privilege. Employees receive only permissions necessary for
their role. Sensitive production access requires approval and periodic access reviews.
AI and Knowledge Systems

AI assistants using internal documents must retrieve information only from sources the requesting user is
authorized to access. Responses should provide source references when possible. Systems must be
evaluated for incorrect retrieval, unsupported answers, prompt injection, and accidental exposure of
confidential information.
Incident Response
For a critical production incident, the on-call engineer should acknowledge the alert, assess customer
impact, and begin mitigation. After restoration, the team conducts a review and tracks corrective actions.
